title: Shield + Hit-recoil + procedural texturing + procedural voice + multiplayer foundation kickoff
notes: Sprint anchors a major MUST-priority kickoff (GDP-009 multiplayer foundation) split across multiple smaller stories, alongside polish from the latest game-design batch.
Multiplayer foundation is the only MUST proposal in flight; we split it into a connect-and-spectate kickoff so the sprint ships in 1-2 days instead of a 2-week monolith.

stories.title: Shield power-up + Hit-recoil animation — one-shot blast protection + visual feedback for the survive case
stories.summary:
Hit-recoil was deferred twice (S105, S106) for a legitimate reason: Kaboom Crew is currently 1-hit-death — no survivable hit exists, so hit-recoil has no trigger. This story unblocks both at once. SHIELD: a fourth power-up kind (`shield`) gives the bomber one-shot blast protection. When a blast that would kill them lands, BomberStats.shield is consumed (true → false), the bomber survives, and HIT-RECOIL fires as the visual signature of that survival. The pair turns the death moment into a readable beat: 'I had a shield, the shield ate the hit, I'm still alive'. Without Shield, the game stays a death-loop; with it, survival becomes a meaningful gameplay event. Visually, the shield bubble (`shield-bubble` shader, already named in visual-style.md §3) appears around the bomber while active and pops on consumption.

Rationale:
Sources: `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md` §5.2 ('Shield reserved name; one-shot blast protection... overlaps in design space with both Kick and Remote') + S105 notes ('hit-recoil deferred — current Kaboom is 1-hit-death, no survival case to recoil from'). Kick (S100) and Remote (S104) have both shipped; Shield was held back per `gameplay-systems.md §5.2` until those two played out. They have. The Shield+Hit-recoil pairing is the logical next step in the survive-a-hit design space and the cheapest path to unblock the hit-recoil dependency.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - SHIELD part:
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/schemas/scene-extensions.schema.json: Pickup.kind enum extended with `shield`. BomberStats gains optional `shield: boolean` (default false). Stacking is binary — either you have a shield or you don't (no shield-up-to-3 like bomb-up).
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/pickup-spawn-system.ts: `shield` in the drop table at ~half the rarity of bomb-up (rough — dev tunes after playtest). Visual: a cyan-glowing dome icon on the cell, distinct silhouette from kick/bomb-up/fire-up/speed-up.
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/pickup-collect-system.ts: `shield` branch sets BomberStats.shield = true. Collecting a second shield while one is active is a NO-OP (silent — no double-stack, no audio).
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/blast-propagation-system.ts (or its damage application path): before flipping alive=false on a hit bomber, check BomberStats.shield. If true, consume it (set to false), emit a `shield-pop` audio event + shield-bubble pop VFX, leave alive=true, fire hit-recoil instead. The bomber stays in place; the round continues.
  -   Friendly-fire interaction: shield consumes for ANY lethal blast — own bomb, opponent bomb, chain reaction. Identity of the bomb owner does not matter for shield consumption.
  -   Multi-blast same frame: if 2+ blasts hit a shielded bomber in the same fixedUpdate, the shield absorbs the FIRST (entity-id-ordered) blast and the bomber dies normally to the second. Tested.
  -   HUD bottom-left bomber line: shows `S` flag when shield is on (mirrors `K` for kick, `R` for remote).
  - VISUAL — shield bubble (shipped alongside the mechanic):
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/shaders/shield-bubble.ts: translucent fresnel-edge sphere around the bomber root, palette.accent (cyan) tinted, opacity ~0.35.
  -   Bubble entity is added as a child of the bomber root when BomberStats.shield flips true; removed when it flips false.
  -   On consumption: a 0.18 s scale-up + opacity-fade tween makes the bubble visibly POP. Reuses the existing Tween primitive.
  - HIT-RECOIL part (the original GDP-2026-05-22-004 part B):
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/anim/hit-recoil-system.ts: NEW. On a BlastEvent that was just absorbed by a bomber's shield (or, forward-compat, any survived blast), schedule a Tween on the bomber's TORSO entity Transform.rotation.x by -8 degrees over 0.10 s, then return to 0 over 0.18 s. Total ~0.28 s.
  -   Hit-recoil writes to the TORSO Transform, not the ROOT — ragdoll uses root. The two never fight because they target different entities.
  -   Hit-recoil is independent of ragdoll: hit-recoil fires when alive STAYS true after a blast (the shield case); ragdoll fires when alive flips false. The two systems share NO state.
  -   Direction: torso pitches AWAY from the blast (same direction logic as ragdoll — read blast origin, derive direction vector, negate the pitch axis). Quick visual telegraph that the bomber got pushed.
  -   Unit tests: hit on shielded bomber → shield consumed + hit-recoil tween fires + bomber stays alive. Hit on unshielded bomber → ragdoll fires + alive=false + hit-recoil does NOT fire. Two rapid shielded hits → shield consumed on first, full ragdoll on second.
  - AUDIO:
  -   New event: `shield-pop` — short crystalline pop sound (when authored). Audio bus integration via the existing audio-binding-system. Vocal-synth (GDP-2026-05-22-008 when it lands) adds a 'hit' slot voice on top.
  - BOT AI:
  -   Bot can collect shield pickup (no special logic). Bot's hit-recoil triggers same as player. NOT in scope: bot AI changing behaviour when shielded (e.g. taking more risks). That's a follow-up if playtest shows it matters.
  - DETERMINISM:
  -   Multi-blast resolution is entity-id-ordered (existing convention). Bot-vs-bot regression test passes — though it may resolve faster on average if bots picked up shields and survived first hits.
  - OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
  -   Multi-charge shield (2-3 hits). HP / health bar mechanics (gameplay-systems.md §7.2 — one-hit kill is the design centre; shield is the exception, not the new rule). Shield expiration on timer. Visual difference per shield charge count (single-shot semantic stays clean). Bot AI shield-awareness. Shield blocking non-blast damage (no other damage source exists in MVP).

Source proposal: GDP-2026-05-22-006 (kind=mechanic, priority=should)
verification: acceptance: Shield power-up + Hit-recoil shipped. Pickup.kind='shield' + BomberStats.shield boolean. pickup-collect sets shield=true (no-op if already true). blast-propagation absorbs lethal blast on shielded bomber: stays alive, shield flips false, no RagdollState, HitRecoilRequest stamped. hit-recoil-system drives \`${rootId}.torso\` Transform.rotation.x through a 0.10s out + 0.18s return ramp (peak ±8°, signed by Z-axis blast direction). Audio: shield-pop AudioEventKind fires on shield true→false edge via procedural sine sweep 900→1700Hz. HUD: bomber line shows compact [KRS] flag suffix.

stories.title: Procedural texturing layer — panel seams + body decals + stripe/spot patterns (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-21-004)
stories.summary:
S102 deferred procedural texturing with the rationale 'no immediate consumer until gameplay shells demand visual variety beyond palette + shape'. That consumer now exists: GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration) put procbomber bombers into Kaboom Crew gameplay, and GDP-2026-05-22-003 added accessories. After playtesting the migrated game, the bombers read as 'a flat-coloured robot' rather than as the industrial-diorama identity the visual-style.md aims at. Adding panel seams + decals + procedural patterns is the highest-value visual upgrade we can ship without an artist. Pure additive layer on top of the existing 8-channel palette + 10-mesh tree.

Rationale:
Source: deferred proposal GDP-2026-05-21-004 (S102 notes: 'deferred — no immediate consumer'). Conditions for un-defer met: migration shipped (S104), accessories shipped (S106), recipe is formalised (S104), bombers are in production gameplay. Visual-style.md §3 declared 9 shader profiles including these layers; this story implements three of them on the character mesh path. Re-promote with acceptance hints rewritten under the post-S106 reality: paint paths now operate on the per-part mesh builders from S102 PROCBOMBER-PART-BUILDERS, not on the merged v0 generator.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Layer 1 — Panel seams (default-on, cheap):
  -   Per-mesh, the 8 corner vertices of each BoxGeometry get the channel colour × 0.85 instead of the full channel; result is a soft 'panel edge' read on every face.
  -   Implementation: extend examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/bomber-parts.ts paintVertexColors() to support a per-vertex Y-position test for the bottom-shadow trick (already there from S102 8-channel palette) PLUS a per-vertex corner test for seams.
  -   Recipe toggle: `recipe.texturing.panelSeams: boolean` (default true). Schema entry added to CharacterRecipe.
  -   Affects ALL part shapes (box / cylinder / capsule) — cylinder + capsule corners are interpreted as 'extreme vertices' (top + bottom edges) and get the same × 0.85 treatment.
  - Layer 2 — Body decals (opt-in, drives identity):
  -   Three starter decals, each implemented as an emissive vertex-colour mask at a fixed anchor on a specific part-mesh:
  -     chestEmblem  — 0.15-wide square centred on the FRONT face of the torso. Emissive = palette.accent.
  -     helmetStripe — horizontal band across the top half of the head's vertical extent. Emissive = palette.accent.
  -     kneePad      — small square on the FRONT face of each lowerLeg's upper third. Emissive = palette.handFoot (non-emissive, just a colour shift).
  -   Each decal adds ONE Float32Array attribute per affected mesh (`decalEmissive`, 1 float per vertex, 0..1).
  -   Shader extension: examples/kaboom-crew/src/shaders/ (or wherever the bomber material lives) gains a `uDecalEmissiveStrength` uniform + the per-vertex attribute sampling. ~30 LOC of GLSL.
  -   Recipe field: `recipe.texturing.decals: ('chestEmblem'|'helmetStripe'|'kneePad')[]` — 0..3 picked deterministically from seed when unspecified.
  - Layer 3 — Stripe / spot patterns (opt-in, family flavour):
  -   Shader-side procedural pattern: a second colour from palette.torsoAccent mixed in at a worley-dot or axial-stripe noise pattern driven by mesh local coordinates.
  -   Stripe = sin(localY * scale) > 0.5 → blend torsoAccent in; otherwise base colour.
  -   Spot = hash(floor(localXZ * scale)) % 4 == 0 → blend torsoAccent.
  -   Solid = no blend (current behaviour).
  -   Recipe field: `recipe.texturing.pattern: { style: 'solid' | 'stripes' | 'spots', scale: 0.5..3.0 } | undefined` (default undefined = solid).
  -   Each palette family in bomber-palette.ts gains a default pattern bias (e.g. `ember` defaults to stripes, `mint` defaults to spots, `slate` stays solid). Recipe can override.
  - Family-default decal selection: each palette family also gains a default decal-pick rule — e.g. `ember` families lean toward `chestEmblem`, `mint` toward `helmetStripe`. Recipe overrides.
  - VALIDATION: recipe.texturing block is fully optional. Within texturing, decals enum strict; pattern.style enum strict; pattern.scale clamped to range. panelSeams is plain boolean.
  - BENCH UI: add three sections to the grouped panel from S103:
  -   'Texturing → Panel seams' (toggle)
  -   'Texturing → Decals' (3 checkboxes)
  -   'Texturing → Pattern' (dropdown solid|stripes|spots + scale slider)
  -   Each control writes to the recipe; rebuild fires the geometry-paint pass.
  - ACCESSORIES INTERACTION: accessories from S106 keep painting from their existing palette channels. The procedural-pattern shader does NOT extend to accessories — accessory meshes stay solid-coloured. Rationale: silhouette readability — decals + patterns on the body itself, accent dots on accessories, the eye doesn't get overloaded.
  - PERFORMANCE:
  -   Vertex attribute additions: one extra Float32Array (`decalEmissive`) per affected mesh. ~24 floats × 6 affected meshes × 4 bombers = 576 extra floats total per arena. Negligible.
  -   Shader uniform additions: 4 new uniforms (uPanelSeamStrength, uDecalEmissive, uPatternStyle, uPatternScale, uPatternColor). All within MeshStandardMaterial onBeforeCompile injection, no new material instance per bomber.
  -   Steady-state per-frame cost is zero — attributes don't re-upload unless the recipe changes.
  - DETERMINISM: same seed + same texturing block → bit-identical vertex-colour + vertex-mask buffers. Test 50 seeds with random texturing combinations.
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST: load two browser tabs with `?recipe=<base64-with-chestEmblem-stripes>` vs `?recipe=<base64-with-helmetStripe-spots>` → the two bombers read as distinct identities at a glance, not just 'two coloured robots'. Manual QA bar, documented in the kaboom-crew README.
  - OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
  -   Normal maps / image textures / UV mapping — visual-style.md §4.3 (no PBR / HDRI / image baking).
  -   Per-accessory texturing — accessories stay solid-coloured for silhouette discipline.
  -   Animated patterns (e.g. flowing emissive lines) — separate shader profile, separate story.
  -   Decal placement editor — anchors are fixed in code, not authorable.
  -   More decal types beyond the 3 — design budget; future decals (`backplate`, `eyeDot`, `armBand` per the deferred-list in GDP-2026-05-21-004) ship one at a time when a specific moment needs them.

stories.title: Research procedural voice synthesis approaches for Kaboom Crew bombers (spike → notes/voice-synth-research.md)
stories.summary: Pure research / spike — no engine code. Survey the practical options for generating short, per-bomber procedural voice clips in the browser via Web Audio API. Goal is to derisk FEAT-PROCEDURAL-VOCAL-SYNTH-S-001 before any system code lands. The output is a single notes/voice-synth-research.md artifact that covers: (a) the design space (formant synthesis, FM, granular, additive, sample-based stretching, ML-tiny vocoders, neural vocoders); (b) what we actually need for Kaboom Crew — 5 short emotional slots (place-bomb / hit / pickup / death / victory), ~80-300 ms each, seed-derived voice colour, deterministic on the same seed, runs cheaply at the existing audio-fx synth bus — and which approaches FIT vs which are over-engineered; (c) concrete references — papers, libraries, demos, open-source projects, JSFXR-style toys, Bfxr / Chiptune approaches, Klang / Tone.js patches, Roli's Equator-style formant chains; (d) one recommended approach to implement first with a sketch of the parameter set (~3-6 seed-derived knobs: base pitch, formant pair F1/F2, envelope attack/decay, harmonic ratio, vowel-like timbre selector); (e) explicit list of what the recommended approach does NOT cover, so the feature story has a clear scope. Constraint: no external dependencies, no pre-rendered audio files, no voice actors, no large model bundles. Everything must run in the same procedural Web Audio path the existing kaboom audio-fx uses.
verification: acceptance: docs/research/voice-synth-research.md exists and covers all six required sections — (1) Kaboom Crew constraints; (2) 8-family design-space comparison table; (3) why formant synthesis specifically + Web Audio recipe; (4) concrete references (papers, OSS projects, game refs); (5) recommended approach with 7 seed-derived knobs + 5 fixed slot envelopes + parameter ranges; (6) explicit out-of-scope list + risks. Names source-filter formant synthesis as primary + additive partials as fallback. The feature story FEAT-PROCEDURAL-VOCAL-SYNTH-S-001 can now proceed with its design pre-locked.
docs/research/voice-synth-research.md: new file (~250 lines)
Survey covers 8 synthesis families; rejects neural / phoneme-TTS / granular / LPC for explicit reasons
Names 7 seed-derived voice-colour knobs (basePitchHz, formantF1Hz, formantF2Hz, formantQ, vibratoHz, vibratoDepth, noiseMix) with numeric ranges
Names 5 fixed emotion slots (place-bomb, hit, pickup, death, victory) with pitch-automation + envelope shape
Cites Klatt 1980, Peterson & Barney 1952, jsfxr, ZzFX, Bfxr, SAM, Tone.js, Bomberman SNES, Mario 64, Hollow Knight

stories.title: Procedural vocal synth — seed-derived per-bomber voice for 5 emotional moments (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-20-010)
stories.summary:
Re-promote of the procedural vocal synth proposal. Original was `could`-priority because it needed several foundations: audio bus (S84, shipped), recipe seed for voice colour derivation (S104, shipped), accessories + ragdoll for richer death + survival moments (S106 + S105, shipped). All foundations in place. Adds a tiny vocal synthesiser that emits short procedural notes at 5 emotional slots — place-bomb, hit (survived via shield), pickup, death (ragdoll launch), victory (round-resolve in this bomber's favour). Voice colour (base pitch, waveform, envelope) derives deterministically from the bomber's recipe seed: seed=42 always sounds like seed=42. All audio generated at play time via Web Audio API — no pre-rendered voice assets, no voice-actor budget. Layered on top of the existing audio clips, never replacing them.

Rationale:
Source: deferred proposal GDP-2026-05-20-010 (still pending in backlog). Conditions for un-defer all now met. Each shipped bomber feature so far gives the bomber visual identity (palette, accessories, body proportions, texturing, ragdoll-on-death). They all SOUND identical though — there's a `bomb-place` clip, but it's the same clip for every bomber regardless of who placed it. Adding a per-bomber voice colour completes the identity-from-seed pipeline: same seed → same look + same sound. Pairs especially well with the survive-a-hit moment from GDP-2026-05-22-006 (Shield) — a hit-but-survived bomber emits a distinct hurt-grunt while the victorious opponent emits their victory note moments later.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Best landed AFTER GDP-2026-05-22-006 (Shield) so the `hit` voice slot has a survivable-hit trigger. If GDP-006 hasn't shipped, the `hit` slot simply doesn't fire and the synth covers 4 slots instead of 5.
  - examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/vocal-synthesis-system.ts: NEW. Subscribes to the existing audio-binding-system event stream. When `bomb-place` / `pickup` / `shield-pop` / `death` (ragdoll alive-flip) / round-resolve-in-this-bomber's-favour fires, the system ALSO emits a short synth note alongside the clip. Clips unchanged — voice is additive.
  - FIVE VOICE SLOTS (each ≤ 0.4 s, monophonic):
  -   place-bomb → 0.15 s downward chirp, peak at slot's basePitchHz, descending fifth.
  -   hit        → 0.12 s sharp 'oof' — fast attack, fast decay, slight pitch dip.
  -   pickup     → 0.18 s upward chirp, peak at +major-third above basePitch.
  -   death      → 0.30 s descending whine timed to land on the ragdoll launch peak (~0.18 s into the ragdoll). Sad, falling-fifth interval.
  -   victory    → 0.40 s rising tritone over the round-resolve fanfare. Single bomber, fires once at RoundState.phase transition to 'won' on this bomber.
  - VOICE COLOUR FROM RECIPE SEED:
  -   examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/voice-color.ts: NEW. Pure function `deriveVoiceColor(recipeSeed: number) => VoiceColor`.
  -   VoiceColor = { basePitchHz: 180..480, waveform: 'sine'|'triangle'|'sawtooth', envelopeAttackMs: 5..30, envelopeReleaseMs: 80..250, vibratoDepthSemitones: 0..0.3 }
  -   Same seed → identical voice colour, every call. Deterministic XOR-shift hash to map seed bits into each field's range.
  - BOT vs PLAYER VOICE BIAS:
  -   Closes the §7.1 open question from characters-and-visual.md ('Bot vocal vs player vocal — same synth or different seed pool?'). Decision: SAME synth, BIASED seed pool.
  -   When an entity is bot-flagged (presence of BotBrain component), the voice-colour resolver shifts the waveform pool toward harsher timbres (saw / triangle weighted 60/30/10 saw/triangle/sine) and the base pitch toward the higher end (300..480).
  -   Player entities (no BotBrain): smoother weighted (sine/triangle/saw 50/40/10), pitch 180..380.
  -   Result: at a glance (ear), the player can tell which voice came from a bot without looking. The recipe seed still wins for individual identity — two bots with different seeds still sound distinct.
  - IMPLEMENTATION (Web Audio API via the existing audio-bus AudioContext):
  -   Each utterance allocates an OscillatorNode + GainNode (envelope) + optional vibrato LFO, schedules them via the audio clock, disconnects them when the envelope completes.
  -   Cap simultaneous utterances at 4 — extra drop silently. In a 4-bomber arena, this means everyone can vocalise at once but pile-ups (death + chain + chain + pickup in same frame) cap out gracefully.
  - OPTIONAL ACCESSIBILITY FLAG:
  -   `?vocals=off` mutes the synth without affecting the existing audio clips. For sound-sensitive players and for robot-playtest determinism (recordings stay clean).
  - UNIT TESTS:
  -   Deterministic: same seed → identical { basePitchHz, waveform, attack, release, vibrato }.
  -   Bot bias: 200 random bot-seeds → ≥ 80% pick saw or triangle waveform. 200 random player-seeds → ≥ 60% pick sine or triangle.
  -   Utterance cap: schedule 10 simultaneous events → only 4 audible nodes created, no exception.
  -   Slot timing: each slot's synth schedule fires within the documented duration window.
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST (manual):
  -   Load `?recipe=<seed=1>` (player) + `?botRecipe=<seed=99>` (bot) → place a bomb in each → the two place-bomb chirps are AUDIBLY different.
  -   Trigger a round-resolve in the player's favour → ONE victory note fires (player's), no victory note for the dead bot.
  -   Trigger a shielded hit (GDP-006 must be shipped) → hit voice fires, bomber still alive, distinct from death whine.
  - OUT OF SCOPE (explicit):
  -   Speech synthesis / phrases / formal taunts. Procedural music. Voice slot customisation per player. Mood shift mid-round (always-the-same-voice keeps the deterministic-by-seed property). Voice mute per individual bomber (only global `?vocals=off` flag).
  -   Adaptive volume mixing (vocal-vs-clip balance) — initial mix is fixed; revisit only if playtest complains.
  -   Real voice acting — explicitly out of art-direction budget per visual-style.md no-artist constraint.

stories.title: Research multiplayer foundation: existing networking stack inventory + connect-and-spectate plan (spike → docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md)
stories.summary: Pure research / spike — no engine code. GDP-009 (FEAT-MULTIPLAYER-FOUNDATION-T-001) is the only MUST story in S109 and the largest in the sprint. It depends on the existing AGF networking stack — the Node reference world server (`examples/backends/node-world-server`), the protocol-schema contracts, the beacon-world client networking adapter, and the engine's WsNetworkAdapterHandle path in `src/app.ts`. None of that has been used by Kaboom Crew yet. This spike inventories what exists, decides whether to reuse it as-is OR fork a kaboom-specific subset, and writes a concrete connect-and-spectate plan in docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md covering: (1) what the Node ref server emits today; (2) which protocol-schema messages Kaboom Crew needs vs which would be over-engineered; (3) where to wire the connection in kaboom-crew bootstrap + the URL surface (`?multiplayer=ws://...` vs auto-discover); (4) the simplest possible spectate slice — two browser tabs see each other's bomber positions in real time, NO shared bomb / blast / pickup state yet; (5) the migration path from spectate to authoritative gameplay (when GDP-009's full scope eventually ships); (6) explicit out-of-scope for THIS spike + for the foundation kickoff. Output: one notes-style .md artifact that lets the feature story open with the design pre-locked, plus a punch-list of follow-up stories (lobby, reconnect, server-authoritative bomb resolution, etc.) that are NOT in S109.
verification: acceptance: docs/research/kaboom-multiplayer-plan.md ships and covers all the required sections — (1) inventory of the existing AGF networking stack (Node ref server ~425 LOC, protocol.schema.json discriminated-union, ws-network-adapter ~522 LOC, beacon-world's 3 connected-profile systems as the reference pattern); (2) the minimum shippable slice (connect-and-spectate: two tabs see each other's bombers move, no shared bombs/blasts/pickups); (3) recommendation between recipe-sync options (Option A: seed-from-playerId, no protocol change); (4) concrete 7-item punch-list for FEAT-MULTIPLAYER-FOUNDATION-T-001; (5) sequencing into 3 commit-sized chunks; (6) explicit hard-perimeter out-of-scope list; (7) 5 named risks with mitigation hints. The feature story can now proceed with its design pre-locked.

stories.title: Multiplayer foundation — two browser tabs share one Kaboom Crew arena via the Node reference server (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-20-007, MUST)
stories.summary:
Re-promote of the original networked-Kaboom proposal. Originally MUST-priority because 'multiplayer is the user's headline goal'. Deferred at the time because too many foundations were missing — recipe wasn't formalised, characters were static, bomb/blast/pickup/round-resolve had not stabilised. All foundations are now shipped: recipe is JSON-serialisable + URL-routable (S104), characters are procedural + deterministic (S102–S106), gameplay state is in well-bounded ECS systems (S82–S108 stacked work). Bomb placement, fuse, blast propagation, block destruction, pickup collection, damage application, round resolution — all are grid-authoritative pure systems with no Math.random / no wall-clock dependencies. This is exactly what AGF's protocol contract expects. Time to stand up the connected profile. Two browser tabs (or two machines) connect to the existing Node reference server (`examples/backends/node-world-server`) and see the same arena, same bombers, same bombs, same outcomes. Server is authoritative; clients predict + reconcile. The single largest leap on the Kaboom Crew roadmap.

Rationale:
Sources: the user's headline 2026-05-20 ask ('modern network game'); original proposal GDP-2026-05-20-007 deferred multiple times; `notes/DynaBomber.md §6` (Multiplayer Model — drop-in/drop-out, server authority, three profiles); `docs/game-design/gameplay-systems.md §9` (deep-dive on authority + reconciliation + drop-in/out). Every other proposal in the recent batches is polish on top of single-player. Without networking, 'modern network game' stays aspirational; with it, the game ARRIVES at its design centre. The migration to a single shared world is the meaning of the whole engine effort to keep gameplay grid-authoritative.

Acceptance hints (game-design proposal — dev to tighten into verification[]):
  - Best treated as a MULTI-SPRINT epic, not a single sprint story. Sprint shape suggestion (dev's call):
  -   Sprint A: protocol + server skeleton + single-client connect (no other players)
  -   Sprint B: 2-client placement + blast + RoundState sync (the headline acceptance)
  -   Sprint C: drop-in/out behaviour + reconnect + spectator-until-next-round
  -   Sprint D: snapshot relevance filter (deferrable — current 15×11 arena fits in a full snapshot)
  -   This story documents the END STATE of Sprint B as the first sprint's acceptance; later sprints have their own focused stories.
  - PROTOCOL (uses the existing protocol schema where possible):
  -   schemas/protocol.schema.json already covers joinWorld / leaveWorld / inputIntent / worldSnapshot from S0-era work. Extend with:
  -     placeBombRequest { entityId, gx, gz, recipeAck?: string } — client → server
  -     detonateRemoteRequest { entityId } — client → server, for the Remote power-up
  -     blastEvent { originGx, originGz, range, ownerId } — server → client (mirror existing component)
  -     pickupCollected { entityId, kind } — server → client
  -     bomberDied { entityId, blastOriginGx, blastOriginGz } — server → client (drives ragdoll on receiving clients)
  -     roundResolved { phase, winnerId?, tally } — server → client
  -     bomberJoined { entityId, recipe: CharacterRecipe } — server → client
  -     bomberLeft { entityId } — server → client
  -   All messages JSON-validated. CharacterRecipe is sent as the canonical JSON shape from GDP-2026-05-22-001.
  - SERVER (examples/backends/node-world-server):
  -   Kaboom Crew rules ship as a server-side module. BombFuseSystem + BlastPropagationSystem + BlockDestructionSystem + PickupCollectSystem + PickupSpawnSystem + RoundResolveSystem all run server-side against an authoritative ECS world.
  -   Server seeds the arena from a configurable world seed; pickup spawn RNG derives from per-cell seed deterministic — same recipe + same world seed → same drops, server-authoritative.
  -   Server runs at fixed tick rate; snapshots emit at ~10 Hz (configurable; lower is fine for 15×11 grid).
  - CLIENT (examples/kaboom-crew):
  -   Connection mode driven by URL: `?world=test&profile=connected` activates the connected profile via the existing ws-network-adapter. `?profile=static` (or no profile flag) stays single-player offline (current behaviour).
  -   In connected profile: bomb-placement / bomb-fuse / blast-propagation / pickup-collect / round-resolve / bot-ai client systems are DISABLED. Client only RENDERS what the server snapshot says.
  -   Local player movement uses client prediction: GridMover updates apply immediately; reconciliation as below.
  -   PlaceBombRequest writes a transient component (already exists for solo); the connected profile routes that intent via the protocol; server validates + spawns the bomb in its world; the next snapshot brings the bomb back.
  - RECONCILIATION (per gameplay-systems.md §9.2):
  -   Server snapshot arrives. Client compares local predicted state with snapshot. If local player grid position differs by ≤ 1 cell, smooth interp toward server value over 200 ms. If > 1 cell, snap. Remote players: interpolate between snapshots; never predict.
  -   Input lag handling: client sends inputIntent with a tick number; server applies at next eligible tick + sends inputAck with resulting state. Client uses ack to trim prediction.
  - DROP-IN / DROP-OUT (per gameplay-systems.md §9.3):
  -   New player at mid-round → spectates until next round (default). Adds them to the joinWorld but holds their bomber spawn until the next RoundResolveSystem-driven reset.
  -   Leaving player → server immediately despawns their bomber. Their live bombs continue to fuse + detonate (server-owned, not client-owned).
  -   Disconnected (network drop, not deliberate leave) → server holds bomber for 5 s grace; reconnect within the window restores. After 5 s, treated as a leave.
  - RECIPE SYNC:
  -   Server is the source of truth for each connected bomber's recipe. Client sends a desired recipe in joinWorld (their `?recipe=` URL); server may accept (default) or override (e.g. an admin scenario forces uniform recipes). Other clients receive the resolved recipe via bomberJoined messages.
  -   Server validates recipes via the same CharacterRecipe schema from GDP-2026-05-22-001 — invalid recipes fall back to a server-seeded default.
  - DETERMINISM:
  -   Server's RNG seeds pickup spawns + bot decisions. Clients trust the server's snapshot. The bot-vs-bot.test.ts SERVER-SIDE continues to pass — running the same gameplay test against the server-hosted world resolves identically.
  -   Client-side determinism is NOT a guarantee post-network — the ragdoll trajectory, vocal-synth scheduling, and visual interpolation are local presentation and may differ between two clients watching the same death. Acceptable.
  - DIAGNOSTICS:
  -   `/__agf/network` probe — peer count, last-snapshot bytes, last-snapshot latency ms, reconciliation jump count.
  -   Doctor section for the connected profile: 'Connected: peer count, snapshot rate, last sync N seconds ago'.
  - BOTS IN MULTIPLAYER:
  -   Server owns BotAISystem. Empty bomber slots in a 2-bomber arena get filled by a server-side bot (default behaviour). Configurable via world config.
  - ACCEPTANCE PLAYTEST (Sprint B END STATE):
  -   TWO playwright tabs join /?project=kaboom-crew&world=test&profile=connected. Both bombers controllable (tab A controls player.1, tab B controls player.2 — or each tab spawns its own bomber).
  -   Tab A places a bomb → tab B sees the bomb spawn within 200 ms.
  -   Tab A's bomb kills tab B's bomber → both tabs see the same ragdoll launch from the same blast direction.
  -   Round resolves → both tabs see the same banner + tally + auto-restart timing.
  -   Tab A reloads (forced disconnect) → tab B sees tab A's bomber held for 5 s grace then despawned.
  - OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS STORY (each is a separate sprint follow-up):
  -   Snapshot-relevance filtering (current arena fits whole snapshot — filter lands when chunked maps do).
  -   Lag compensation / hit-detection rewind (no hitscan weapons — bombs are slow-fuse, lag tolerable).
  -   Server reconnect-resume after server restart.
  -   Custom rooms / lobbies / matchmaking.
  -   Anti-cheat / authentication.
  -   Cross-server world federation.
  -   Persistent player profile across server restarts (the cosmetic-unlock plan waits for this).
  - EPIC FLIP: examples/kaboom-crew/README.md roadmap table flips KABOOM-CREW-MVP-NETWORK from 'planned' to 'active' when Sprint A starts.
